result:
Solution 1 is wrong. Its answer $c=1$ gives $n \le 2m-2$ at $k=3$, which is weaker than the existing bound $2m-3$, so it cannot be a refinement. The solution also admits it is guessing from the form of the bound.

Solution 2 is wrong. Its own check shows that a refinement requires $c \ge 3$, and it then reports $c=2$ anyway. Its self-correction notes that $c=2$ gives $2m-2$, which is not a refinement, but it still settles on 2 with no valid justification.

Solution 3 gives $c=3$, which matches the requirement. The bound $2m-\lfloor (k+3)/2\rfloor$ equals $2m-3$ at $k=3$ and is strictly stronger for $k \ge 5$, so it refines $n \le 2m-3$. The derivation is plausible: the dual-space condition gives $d \ge n-m+2$, and combining this with the rank-metric Singleton bound $km \le n(m-d+1)$ yields $k \lesssim 2(j-1)$ for $n=2m-j$, i.e. $j \ge \lceil k/2\rceil+1 = \lfloor (k+3)/2\rfloor$. I did not verify every step of the geometric argument or the sharpness claim, so my confidence is moderate rather than certain. Note that $c=4$ also agrees with $2m-3$ at $k=3$, so the "refines" condition alone does not rule it out. I am relying on recollection of the literature result for $c=3$.

VERDICT 1: REJECT
VERDICT 2: REJECT
VERDICT 3: ACCEPT
